title: Outage: the app subnet's default route still points at last night's retired appliance

brief.situation: You are the network engineer for Halden Mutual, a fictional insurer on Azure with a hub-and-spoke network. Last night change CHG-2291 replaced the third-party firewall appliance in the hub (fw-nva01, 10.0.1.4) with Azure Firewall. Since then the claims servers in spoke subnet snet-app cannot reach the card processor at pay.example.net. Claims payouts settle in a batch at 11:00. Policy: all spoke egress goes through the hub firewall.
handover: Route table rt-app is associated with snet-app (10.20.1.0/24); the hub VNet is peered with the spoke.
Azure Firewall afw-hub already has an application rule allowing pay.example.net from 10.20.0.0/16.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the diagram shows the claims VM, its route table, the hub and the card processor.
Each command takes a minute or two; the clock moves only when you act or wait.
When you close, you write the record and explain your reasoning.

source.note: The payout batch settles at 11:00, 45 minutes after the report.

nextHop.why: Wait for the running command to finish.

effects.finding: A user-defined route in rt-app sends the card processor's traffic to 10.0.1.4, the appliance CHG-2291 retired.

Default   Active   10.20.0.0/16     VnetLocal
Default   Active   10.0.0.0/16      VNetPeering
{bypass ? "Default   Active   0.0.0.0/0        Internet" : routeFixed ? "User      Active   0.0.0.0/0        VirtualAppliance  10.0.1.68
Default   Invalid  0.0.0.0/0        Internet" : "User      Active   0.0.0.0/0        VirtualAppliance  10.0.1.4
Default   Invalid  0.0.0.0/0        Internet"}

effects.finding: The user route 0.0.0.0/0 overrides the system default route: every outbound flow goes to the next hop it names.

effects.finding: The firewall that replaced the appliance listens on 10.0.1.68.

changeLog.why: Wait for the running command to finish.

effects.finding: CHG-2291 deallocated fw-nva01 and created afw-hub; nothing touched rt-app in the spoke.

fixRoute.label: az network route-table route update -g rg-claims --route-table-name rt-app -n default-egress --next-hop-type VirtualAppliance --next-hop-ip-address 10.0.1.68

effects.output:
netops@cloudshell:~$ az network route-table route update -g rg-claims --route-table-name rt-app -n default-egress --next-hop-type VirtualAppliance --next-hop-ip-address 10.0.1.68 -o table
AddressPrefix    NextHopIpAddress    NextHopType       ProvisioningState
0.0.0.0/0        10.0.1.68           VirtualAppliance  Succeeded

effects.log: Spoke egress goes to Azure Firewall again, where the pay.example.net rule already allows it.

deleteRoute.label: az network route-table route delete -g rg-claims --route-table-name rt-app -n default-egress
deleteRoute.available: not busy and (not bypass and not routeFixed)

effects.output:
netops@cloudshell:~$ az network route-table route delete -g rg-claims --route-table-name rt-app -n default-egress
(no output)

effects.log: The system route sends spoke traffic straight to the internet: payouts work, and nothing inspects or logs them.

nsgAllow.label: az network nsg rule create --nsg-name nsg-app ... --priority 100 --direction Outbound --access Allow --destination-address-prefixes Internet

effects.output:
netops@cloudshell:~$ az network nsg rule create -g rg-claims --nsg-name nsg-app -n allow-out-any --priority 100 --direction Outbound --access Allow --destination-address-prefixes Internet
"provisioningState": "Succeeded"

effects.log: A new allow rule changes nothing: the NSG was not blocking; the route sends packets to an address that no longer answers.

writeup.question: For the record: where the packets went, what you changed, and how you know it holds.

parts.label: Where
parts.criteria: Uses next hop and effective routes to show the user route and its dead next hop.
parts.modelAnswer: Next hop and the NIC's effective routes showed a user route 0.0.0.0/0 to VirtualAppliance 10.0.1.4, the appliance CHG-2291 deallocated; nothing was wrong with the NSG or the firewall rule.

parts.label: Change
parts.criteria: Points the route at the new firewall rather than removing it, keeping egress inspected.
parts.modelAnswer: Updated rt-app's default-egress route to 10.0.1.68, Azure Firewall's private IP, so egress still goes through the hub as policy requires; deleting the route would have sent it straight to the internet.

parts.label: Holds
parts.criteria: Verifies the path and the firewall's log before 11:00.
parts.modelAnswer: Connection troubleshoot reported Reachable and AZFWApplicationRule showed 10.20.1.10 allowed to pay.example.net before the batch.

expertPath.text: Next hop: VirtualAppliance 10.0.1.4 from rt-app; effective routes: the user 0.0.0.0/0 route is active; the activity log: fw-nva01 deallocated by CHG-2291.
Azure Firewall's private IP is 10.0.1.68; update the route's next hop to it.
Connection troubleshoot: Reachable; AZFWApplicationRule shows the claims server allowed.

bypass.headline: It works, around the firewall
bypass.body: Without the user route the system route sends 0.0.0.0/0 to the internet. Payouts flowed, uninspected and unlogged. Point the route at the new firewall's private IP instead.

batchMissed.headline: The batch could not reach the processor
batchMissed.body: Restarts and NSG rules do not change where a user route sends packets. Next hop and effective routes name the route and its next hop in one command.

fixed.headline: Good: the route, not the symptoms
fixed.body: You found the user route with next hop, took the new firewall's IP from the firewall itself, changed only that route, and proved it with connection troubleshoot and the firewall's own log.

gaps.headline: Fixed, with gaps
gaps.body: The criteria show what was left: the diagnosis, the firewall's IP, the broad NSG rule, or the checks.

time_up.headline: Time up
time_up.body: No record was written before the run's hard limit.

scoring.modelReasoning: Next hop for the card processor's address returns VirtualAppliance 10.0.1.4 from route table rt-app, and the NIC's effective routes show that user route overriding the system default route. CHG-2291 deallocated fw-nva01 at that address and built Azure Firewall at 10.0.1.68, but nobody changed the spoke's route. Update the route's next hop to the firewall's private IP; deleting it would restore payouts by sending them straight to the internet, around the firewall policy requires. NSG rules and restarts do not change routing. Verify with connection troubleshoot and the firewall's application rule log before 11:00.
